items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Well, there was me... And then they had... Leroy Maxey on drums.

ctx.x: Well, there was me, I was the added saxophone. Had Orville Harris on alto, Andy Brown on alto and Walter Thomas on tenor. Then they had Lamar Wright on trumpet, Doc Cheetham on trumpet and Edwin Swazey on trumpet. Then they had De Priest Wheeler on trombone and Harry White

on trombone. And Benny Payne was on piano, Al Morgan on bass, Maurice White on guitar and Leroy Maxey on drums. And then later when Edwin Swazey died Irving Randolph took his place. And then later on Keg (DOMESTIC) Johnson came in the band in Harry White's place. And then we added another trombone which was Claude Jones. And then Ben Webster took Orville Harris' place so we had two tenors and two altos then. And that's how the band was when I left the band in '35.

But anyway, we went to California. This is the first time, I think, Cab had gone to California. That's when I stayed out in California. But we went out there and played up and down the coast, in Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club, then we made a picture with Al Jolson, "The Singing Kid."
